label: Formulated endopsychic structure based on object-seeking libido and ego splitting
description: Fairbairn replaced Freud's id-ego-superego with a dynamic structural model composed of Central Ego, Libidinal Ego, and Anti-Libidinal Ego.
historicalContext: Published in 'A Revised Psychopathology of the Psychoses and Psychoneuroses' (1941) and 'Endopsychic Structure' (1944).
dialecticalTension: Libido is essentially object-seeking, not pleasure-seeking; pleasure is a signpost toward relational connection.

citations.author: W.R.D. Fairbairn
citations.sectionOrPage: Chapter 4: Endopsychic Structure Considered in Terms of Object-Relationships

label: Overturned Freud's tension-reduction drive theory in favor of an inherently object-seeking libido
description: Fairbairn directly refuted Freud's hedonistic pleasure principle, arguing that impulses cannot be separated from object relations.
historicalContext: Fairbairn's papers written in Edinburgh during the 1940s marked a radical departure from classical energy mechanics.
dialecticalTension: Energy and structure are inseparable: energy is an inherent attribute of ego structures seeking human objects.

citations.author: Jay R. Greenberg and Stephen A. Mitchell

label: Fairbairn's pure object-relations model provided the cornerstone for Relational Psychoanalysis
description: Stephen Mitchell identified Fairbairn as the purest relational theorist in the psychoanalytic tradition.
historicalContext: Mitchell made Fairbairn the central pivot of his 1983 treatise 'Object Relations in Psychoanalytic Theory'.
dialecticalTension: Translating Fairbairn's intrapsychic internalized bad objects into active relational enactments.

citations.author: Jay R. Greenberg and Stephen A. Mitchell

label: Endopsychic ego splitting and internalized object units informed Kernberg's structural diagnosis
description: Kernberg integrated Fairbairn's structural units of self-representation, object-representation, and connecting affect into his borderline theory.
historicalContext: Kernberg synthesized Fairbairn with Freud and Klein in 'Internal World and External Reality' (1980).
dialecticalTension: Reconciling Fairbairn's object-seeking structure with Freudian biological drive foundations.
